fixed_rules: CONTRADICTED, NOT_ENOUGH_EVIDENCE and ERROR always require human review
SUPPORTED on weak evidence (no accepted citation from the top-ranked passage) requires human review
a missing source or conflicting references give NOT_ENOUGH_EVIDENCE, never SUPPORTED
a policy can add review reasons to SUPPORTED claims, never remove one (ClaimResult contract)
no model confidence is used: none is requested, and a reply carrying one is refused

calibration.reason: No model-backed outcomes exist yet, so nothing has been tuned. The defaults follow the stated rule: avoid auto-clearing a claim that is not true before reducing review volume. 'strong' auto-clears a SUPPORTED claim only when code verified more than the model's word (its figures matched in the quotes, or two or more accepted citations from the top-ranked passage); a figure-free claim on one quote goes to a person. Compound claims need two accepted citations.

limitations.finding: Text extraction (pypdf, backend) keeps a table's rows only when the PDF writes them row by row. For a column-ordered table every column comes out as a block, so a product loses its figures, and a model that pairs a product with the wrong row's figure gets a SUPPORTED the citation guard cannot refuse. Measured on one hand-built PDF of each kind; real PDFs vary.

A reference over 1,000,000 characters, or more than 50 references, is refused rather than truncated. On the 1,144-word product handbook, top-5 token-chunk retrieval keeps 100% recall but sends about 89% of the corpus to the verifier, so long documents cost more and expose the model to more look-alike facts.

The negation check, retrieval stopwords and unit words are English only: a Portuguese claim that drops 'não' is not caught by the negation check. Prompts are English; a live model on other languages is untested, and the dataset is English only.

Retrieval is lexical (BM25): a claim worded differently from its evidence ('cost €99' vs 'Price: €129') can retrieve nothing, and '12 hours' is not matched to 'twelve hours', so a correct claim is downgraded to NOT_ENOUGH_EVIDENCE (safe, but a missed confirmation).

The property-binding (property_mismatch) and compound-claim (unsupported_clause) checks are lexical heuristics, not validated. They were tuned on the Round 3 step 03/04 matrix cases, the REG-014/015 tests and dev records v1-036/v1-045; of 12 probes checked afterwards, only 4 were written after the final rules, and one other probe shaped the rule for figures of different units. They are untested on fresh data until steps 06/07. Words match exactly: a synonym is accepted rather than checked ('stays chilled for up to 12 hours' passes on 'cold for up to 24 hours and hot for up to 12 hours'), a correct claim worded like another unit's label can be falsely rejected ('a 2 year guarantee that covers the battery' next to 'Battery life: up to 12 hours'), and a claim part paraphrased in new words can be refused. Two earlier limits, the elision swap and a part covered by one incidental shared word, are now caught.
A false fact written as ordinary text in a reference is evidence like any other: only instructions aimed at a model are refused. References must be trusted when they are approved.

limitations.topic: Guard on a comparative claim across documents
limitations.finding: The guard can reject a correct SUPPORTED answer whose claim compares figures that come from two documents. Held-out record v4-003 ('the Lantern's warranty is longer than the standard 2 year warranty', with the 3 year figure in one document and the 2 year figure in another) is rejected as property_mismatch even with the right gold quotes. It was found the first time the oracle ran on this fresh held-out record (2026-10-29), so the rule was deliberately not changed and the record was not replaced: held-out records do not steer the rules. It is a false rejection (a person reviews it), not a wrong approval.

limitations.topic: Retrieval on a claim that carries an injected instruction
limitations.finding: The retrieval-only evaluation uses the whole claim text as one query. On the 120-record dataset, 2 of 87 records with evidence (v4-024 held-out, v4-040 dev) retrieve no passage, because the claim itself contains an injected instruction whose words dilute the query below the term-coverage threshold; the same claim without that sentence retrieves its passage. Recall@5 is 85/87 (was 37/37 on the 80-record dataset), so the gate was re-measured, lower, because the dataset grew. The full pipeline extracts claims before retrieval and may avoid this; that is not measured until the live run.

One live run (google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite, verifier only, 80 synthetic claims, 25 held out) gave CONTRADICTED recall 87.5% (28/32), precision 90.3%, false-positive rate 6.2%, and citation validity 86.7% (52/60), which misses the 100% gate; every quote was found verbatim (60/60). It is one run on AI-written labels (0/80 reviewed), so read it as an indication, not a guarantee; the full pipeline (extraction and routing) was not run live.

Every label in eval/dataset.jsonl was written by an AI assistant and checked mechanically; none has been reviewed by a person (0/120). The data is synthetic (a fictional company) and small: one CONTRADICTED record is about 2 points of recall (1/49).

Deterministic terminology, brand-compliance and accessibility rules exist (rules.py) and are unit tested, but they are not part of the labelled dataset, so this report says nothing about them. Accessibility checks read only Markdown/HTML in the submitted text and the metadata given: images, colours and media inside uploaded files are not inspected (those checks report not_checkable; the backend passes no ContentMetadata yet).
Images themselves (logos, product photos), brand tone of voice and reading level are not checked; only all-caps and emoji runs are flagged as tone signals.

The backend applies the engine's decision policy to every claim (services/api engine/pipeline.py, _with_decision_policy), so a weak or under-cited SUPPORTED claim goes to a person. This evaluation does not measure that routing: it is tested only by the backend suite (services/api/tests/test_decision_policy.py), which needs PostgreSQL and runs in CI. An earlier entry here said the backend routed on verdict != SUPPORTED only; that was out of date.
